::: {.teacher-key}
This key checks the original classroom model, not a particular physical relay or
horn. Verify actual coil resistance, contact layout, lamp ratings, horn current,
fuse size, conductor size, and supply limits before construction.
:::

## Relay-state table

| Condition | Coil energized? | Connected contact | Loads that operate |
|---|---|---|---|
| State A: S1 open | No | 30 to 87a | L1 |
| State B: S1 closed | Yes | 30 to 87 | L2 and H1 |

## 1. State A path

Positive 12 V source → F1 → terminal 30 → closed 87a contact → L1 → 0 V
return → source. Terminal 87 is open, so the L2/horn branch has no source path.

## 2. State B paths

Coil: positive 12 V control branch → F2 → S1 → terminal 86 → K1 coil →
terminal 85 → return.

Load branches: positive 12 V load branch → F1 → terminal 30 → terminal 87 →
branch node. One branch continues through L2 to return; the other continues
through H1 to return. Terminal 87a is open, so L1 is off.

## 3. Coil current and power

$$
I_{COIL}=\frac{V}{R}=\frac{12.0\ \mathrm{V}}{80.0\ \Omega}=0.150\ \mathrm{A}
$$

$$
P_{COIL}=VI=(12.0)(0.150)=1.80\ \mathrm{W}
$$

## 4. Coil-loop KVL

Using ideal F2 and S1:

$$
+12.0-V_{F2}-V_{S1}-V_{COIL}=0
$$

Therefore $V_{COIL}=12.0$ V from TP1 to TP2, and each ideal closed fuse,
switch, or wire has 0 V drop.

<div class="page-break"></div>

## 5. Lamp current

For either lamp at its rating:

$$
I_L=\frac{P}{V}=\frac{21.0\ \mathrm{W}}{12.0\ \mathrm{V}}=1.75\ \mathrm{A}
$$

## 6. State A current and KVL

Only L1 is energized, so $I_{30}=I_{L1}=1.75$ A.

$$
+12.0-V_{F1}-V_{30\rightarrow87a}-V_{L1}=0
$$

With ideal protection and contacts, $V_{L1}=12.0$ V.

## 7. State B KCL and horn power

At the node after terminal 87:

$$
I_{30}=I_{L2}+I_H
$$

$$
I_H=6.50-1.75=4.75\ \mathrm{A}
$$

The parallel horn has 12.0 V across it:

$$
P_H=VI=(12.0)(4.75)=57.0\ \mathrm{W}
$$

## 8. Total battery current and power

If both fused branches use the same battery:

$$
I_{BAT}=I_{30}+I_{COIL}=6.50+0.150=6.65\ \mathrm{A}
$$

$$
P_{BAT}=VI=(12.0)(6.65)=79.8\ \mathrm{W}
$$

The load branch accounts for 78.0 W and the coil for 1.80 W.

## 9. Meter placement

Voltage across L2: red probe at the L2 positive terminal supplied from 87; black
probe at the L2 return terminal. A DC clamp for horn current surrounds the horn
supply conductor or horn return conductor alone—not both.

<div class="page-break"></div>

## 10. Poor-ground calculation

Modelled hot lamp resistance:

$$
R_{L1}=\frac{V^2}{P}=\frac{(12.0)^2}{21.0}=6.857\ \Omega\approx6.86\ \Omega
$$

With the 1.00 Ω fault:

$$
R_T=6.857+1.00=7.857\ \Omega
$$

$$
I=\frac{12.0}{7.857}=1.527\ \mathrm{A}\approx1.53\ \mathrm{A}
$$

$$
V_{L1}=IR=(1.527)(6.857)=10.47\ \mathrm{V}
$$

$$
V_{FAULT}=I(1.00)=1.527\ \mathrm{V}\approx1.53\ \mathrm{V}
$$

KVL check: $10.47+1.53=12.00$ V.

## 11. Faulted lamp power

$$
P_{L1}=I^2R=(1.527)^2(6.857)=16.0\ \mathrm{W}
$$

This is below 21.0 W, so the model predicts a dimmer lamp. The 1.00 Ω fault
dissipates approximately 2.33 W. Real lamp resistance is temperature-dependent,
so a physical reading will not exactly match this fixed-resistance model.

## 12. Diagnostic conclusion

A 1.53 V reading from lamp ground to battery negative while current flows shows
excess voltage drop on the ground side. The supported fault region is the lamp
ground connection, return conductor, connector, or chassis bond between the
lamp and battery negative. Power off, isolate the source, and inspect/tighten the
ground-side terminals and conductor before using resistance or continuity mode.

## Independent agreement checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| State B branch current | $1.75+4.75=6.50$ A |
| State B power | $21.0+57.0=78.0$ W |
| Source load power | $12.0\times6.50=78.0$ W |
| Poor-ground KVL | $10.47+1.53=12.00$ V |
| Poor-ground power | $16.0+2.33\approx18.33$ W |
| Faulted source power | $12.0\times1.527\approx18.33$ W |
